title: Multiplayer Crane Claw Machine
prompt:
Create a single HTML file with a multiplayer crane claw machine game using Three.js and GLTFLoader. Load 'BoxAnimated.glb' using GLTFLoader from CDN (https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.160.0/examples/jsm/loaders/GLTFLoader.js). Use Three.js from https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.160.0/build/three.module.js via importmap.

## Scene Setup
- Glass-walled claw machine cabinet: a transparent box (width=8, height=10, depth=6) centered at origin, with MeshPhysicalMaterial (transmission=0.5, roughness=0.1)
- Floor of the cabinet at y=0 with a green felt-like material
- Two crane assemblies mounted on overhead rails at y=9:
  - Player 1 (P1): Red crane claw, starts at x=-2, z=0. Controlled by WASD + Space
  - Player 2 (P2): Blue crane claw, starts at x=2, z=0. Controlled by Arrow keys + Enter
- Each claw has 3 prongs modeled as thin cones that open/close during grab animation
- Load 'BoxAnimated.glb' and place 6 instances as prizes scattered on the floor at known positions: [(-2,0.5,-1), (-1,0.5,1), (0,0.5,-1.5), (1,0.5,0.5), (2,0.5,-0.5), (0,0.5,1.5)]. Scale each to 0.5. Play the embedded animation on each box using AnimationMixer.
- Camera: PerspectiveCamera at (0, 8, 14) looking at (0, 4, 0)
- Lights: AmbientLight(0xffffff, 0.4), two SpotLights (one warm, one cool) from above pointing down, plus colorful PointLights inside the cabinet for arcade feel
- A prize chute on each side: left for P1 (x=-5), right for P2 (x=5), modeled as simple ramps

## Physics & Mechanics (custom, no physics engine)
- Each crane can move horizontally on X and Z within cabinet bounds (x: -3.5 to 3.5, z: -2.5 to 2.5) at speed 3 units/sec
- When a player presses grab (Space for P1, Enter for P2), the claw descends from y=9 to y=1.5 over 1 second, closes prongs, then ascends back. During descent/ascent, horizontal movement is locked.
- Grab success: if claw center is within 1.0 unit (Euclidean XZ distance) of any uncollected prize center when claw reaches bottom, the prize attaches to the claw. There's a 70% grab success rate (use seeded random: Math.random() < 0.7 at grab moment).
- If grab succeeds, prize moves with claw up. At top, claw moves to the player's chute (P1 to x=-4, P2 to x=4) and drops the prize. Prize is then marked as collected by that player.
- If grab fails (distance too far or 30% random fail), claw ascends empty.
- Collision between cranes: if both cranes are within 1.5 units of each other on XZ plane, they repel each other by 0.5 units along the vector between them.

## Scoring & Game State
- Each prize is worth 10 points. First to 30 points wins (or highest score when all 6 prizes collected).
- Display a HUD with:
  - P1 score (top-left, red text, id='p1-score')
  - P2 score (top-right, blue text, id='p2-score')
  - Game status (top-center, id='game-status'): 'PLAYING', 'P1 WINS!', 'P2 WINS!', or 'TIE!'
  - Timer counting up in seconds (id='game-timer')
  - A 'Reset Game' button (id='reset-btn') that resets everything
  - Prize count remaining (id='prizes-left')

## State Management
Expose window.__3D_STATE__ with:
- p1: { x, y, z, score, isGrabbing, hasPrize, clawState: 'idle'|'descending'|'ascending'|'moving_to_chute' }
- p2: { x, y, z, score, isGrabbing, hasPrize, clawState: 'idle'|'descending'|'ascending'|'moving_to_chute' }
- prizes: array of 6 objects { x, y, z, collected: bool, collectedBy: null|1|2 }
- prizesRemaining: number (0-6)
- gameStatus: 'PLAYING'|'P1 WINS!'|'P2 WINS!'|'TIE!'
- gameTime: number (seconds elapsed, float)
- craneCollisionCount: number of times cranes collided
- totalGrabAttempts: number
- successfulGrabs: number
- animationsPlaying: boolean (true if BoxAnimated animations are running)

Update __3D_STATE__ every frame in the animation loop.
physics_constraints: Cranes bounded within cabinet (x: -3.5 to 3.5, z: -2.5 to 2.5). Claw descent from y=9 to y=1.5 in ~1 second. Grab detection radius 1.0 unit in XZ. 70% grab success probability. Crane-crane repulsion at distance < 1.5 units. Prizes have gravity when dropped into chute. No NaN values in any position or score.
